source.title: Architecture-aware minimization (A2M): how to find flat minima in neural architecture search
source.authors: Matteo Gambella; Fabrizio Pittorino; Manuel Roveri

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper builds A2M by applying a SAM-like flatness update to architecture parameters and reports the method's outcomes. It does not test any listed claim version about fitting random labels, width, convolutional bias, optimizer or batch comparisons, dropout, weight-space sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports architecture-space neighborhoods, accuracy barriers, and test-accuracy comparisons for A2M and standard NAS methods. These do not measure any listed version's behavior. Cited results about weight-space sharpness and other methods are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study applies a SAM-like update to NAS architecture parameters and evaluates architecture geometry and its own method's accuracy. Its flatness measures concern changes in architectures and test-accuracy barriers, whereas V7 concerns magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and train–test gaps. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that high-performing architectures cluster in flatter architecture-space regions and that A2M improves generalization across several NAS methods and benchmarks. This should retain the qualification that improvements are not universal: Table 2 includes unchanged results and decreases, including SDARTS-RS on NAS-Bench-201 ImageNet-16-120, DARTS- on DARTS CIFAR-100, and PC-DARTS on DARTS ImageNet-16-120.
record.recipe_differences: Architecture-aware minimization changes the DARTS architecture-parameter gradient using a SAM-like update; it does not test the listed versions' original interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: A2M performance is sensitive to the architecture-neighborhood radius ρα; the authors report different optimal values for NAS-Bench-201 and DARTS.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected high-performing NAS-Bench-201 architecture pairs have lower test-accuracy path barriers than medium- and low-performing pairs across three datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-performing architectures can occupy flatter regions of discrete architecture space.

fits_no_version.finding: A2-DARTS has smaller worst sampled radius-1 neighbor accuracy drops than DARTS: 0.67 versus 0.81 percentage points on CIFAR-10 and 0.90 versus 2.88 on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A2-DARTS can find architectures whose immediate architecture neighborhoods better preserve test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Reported aggregate test accuracies increase from 90.95 to 94.54, 70.66 to 75.26, and 44.06 to 47.70 across methods and both search spaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A2M improves average test accuracy across the reported NAS comparisons, with individual exceptions.

record.problems: NAS-Bench-201 geometry is benchmark-query based, while DARTS neighbor studies use 30 sampled architectures and early stopping at a fixed training-loss threshold; ImageNet-16-120 DARTS neighborhoods were not analyzed. The aggregate accuracy rows do not establish effects for each individual method.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports method-by-method test accuracies in Table 2 and validation accuracies in Table 7, as well as additional neighborhood distributions and Kolmogorov–Smirnov results in Appendix D. These are not extracted row-by-row because they evaluate the A2M method or architecture-space geometry and do not measure any listed version.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.

Magnitude-scaled weight sharpness, its association with train–test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. Comparable training-loss thresholds for architecture neighbors do not establish these results.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Architecture-space flatness is a related but distinct construct from V7. Adam and SGD are used for different parameter blocks without an optimizer comparison; batch sizes, widths, and drop-path settings are recipe details without the interventions needed to test V2, V4, V5, or V6. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
